subject.title: [Feature]: When messages are merged and processed, the agent event is expected to carry the original runId(s)

question: What public Gateway event contract should represent source-run lineage when multiple chat.send requests merge into one executed agent run?
rationale: Current code can identify queued turns and collect-mode groups, but the fix requires a stable API choice about field naming, ordering, duplicate handling, and whether public runId should remain the execution ID or become one of the source IDs.

options.title: Add an ordered lineage array
options.body: Keep runId as the executed run ID and add an ordered originalRunIds/sourceRunIds-style field to public agent/chat events for merged work.

options.title: Reuse one source run ID
options.body: Make merged execution use the first or last queued run ID as the public runId, which helps simple clients but loses full lineage.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave clients to correlate through accepted responses, session state, and history, accepting that merged live events do not expose all source run IDs.

recommendation.title: Add an ordered lineage array
recommendation.body: Keep runId as the executed run ID and add an ordered originalRunIds/sourceRunIds-style field to public agent/chat events for merged work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history signal for collect-mode queue semantics and Gateway event/run lifecycle behavior, and the issue timeline routed this decision to them.
